ARCH 201.name: Architectural Design Studio I
ARCH 201.description: Introduction to principles and concepts of architectural design; case study and analysis; small-scaled projects on specific design problems. Development of skills in architectural representation.

ARCH 202.name: Architectural Design Studio II
ARCH 202.description: Exploration of the relationship between the building and the site. Integration of basic urban concepts into the design process in the context of urban design and development.

ARCH 221.name: Fundamentals of Architecture
ARCH 221.description: Architectonic elements, concepts of form and space, basic organization principles, geometrical relationships and circulation. Space/place ethics and social production of space. Contemporary and historical built examples. Works and philosophies of contemporary architects.

ARCH 231.name: Statics and Strength of Materials
ARCH 231.description: Introduction to the basic concepts and principles of statics; vector mechanics; geometrical properties; free body diagrams; internal forces: shear and moment diagrams. Analysis of simple load-carrying structures; columns; concepts of stress, strain and deformation.

ARCH 251.name: Architectural Building Systems
ARCH 251.description: Introduction to construction materials, their properties, production and construction methods, application and use in architecture; integration of design and building technology; building sustainability; development of a set of detail drawings.

ARCH 252.name: Construction and Materials
ARCH 252.description: Continuation of ARCH 251. Integration of building construction elements, methods, materials and technology; understanding of building components, such as roofs, walls, floors and stairs as systems; analysis of traditional and current building technologies; communication of construction ideas and details through visual tools and proper graphic representation. Development of a set of construction document drawings.

ARCH 290.name: Summer Practice I
ARCH 290.description: Practical experience in building construction processes; active participation in construction work on site (4 weeks).

ARCH 301.name: Architectural Design Studio III
ARCH 301.description: Investigation of functional complexity, spatial variety, aesthetic and technological components of buildings. Creative interpretation of the concepts of environmental sustainability and building design.

ARCH 302.name: Architectural Design Studio IV
ARCH 302.description: Exploration of collaborative design. Integration of architectural, interior and urban design concepts.

ARCH 315.name: Computerized Presentation Techniques
ARCH 315.description: Advanced usage of computerized programs for representation of projects by integrating traditional and computer media.

ARCH 316.name: Programming in Architecture
ARCH 316.description: This course explores the role of computation in the conception and representation of geometry. Participants will develop, analyze and critique algorithmic approaches to digital drawing and modeling utilizing Python Rhinoscript library. This library allows Rhinoceros -3D graphics and computer-aided design (CAD) modeling software- to be scripted with text-based coding. Scripting in this manner can (i) Automate analog processes, (ii) Reveals vast form finding potential.

ARCH 317.name: Parametric Design Studio
ARCH 317.description: Different parameters of design are examined; skills are acquired in establishing building information systems (BIMs) and using them efficiently through the utilization of related software packages.

ARCH 318.name: (Ar)chitectural Visualization
ARCH 318.description: This courses introduces the students with the state-of-the art media and tools for visualization of architecture. The aim is to get familiar with the multitude of tools, applications and software used for augmented reality and test how they may be used for architectural design presentations.

ARCH 321.name: Architecture and Society
ARCH 321.description: Investigation of societal and environmental aspects and determinants of architectural design; analysis of case studies.

ARCH 331.name: Structural Design I
ARCH 331.description: Principal structural elements of a building: Beams, columns and slabs. Load distributions on the structure. Exploring material properties and deformation. Introduction to steel; structural design of steel elements. Analysis of architectural applications. Case studies of historic and contemporary steel structures.

ARCH 332.name: Structural Design II
ARCH 332.description: Introduction to concrete, design and analysis of reinforced concrete members. Exploring pre-stressed and post tension techniques. Case studies of historic and contemporary examples. Earthquake: Importance and role in structural design. Introduction to finite element modeling (FEM) and computer analysis.

ARCH 333.name: Form and Structure
ARCH 333.description: Provides an understanding of the behavior of structures in relation to their form; studies spatial structures such as shells, domes, cable-nets and fabrics using computer programs where the relationship between the geometrical form and the structural behavior will be observed and explained through structural simulations.

ARCH 341.name: Architectural Lighting and Acoustics
ARCH 341.description: Study of fundamental daylight and artificial lighting principles; building lighting performance; lighting design methods. Introduction to concepts of architectural acoustics; sound behavior in buildings; noise control; fundamental design principles and methods. Fire prevention in buildings; life-safety systems and architectural applications; standards and regulations.

ARCH 342.name: Environmental Technologies and Artificial Intelligence Based Analysis
ARCH 342.description: Introduction to contemporary mechanical systems and equipment for heating, cooling, ventilation and plumbing. Consideration of environmental sustainability. Integration of water supply and heating systems into the building design; waste water disposal; electrical systems, wiring. Evaluation of building service systems performance; technical drawings and documentation of the proposed designs.

ARCH 351.name: Urban Metabolism: tools from the social sciences for architects and designers
ARCH 351.description: City as a dynamic, contested space, marked by reconfiguration and change. Literatures of actor-network theory, urban political ecology, urban regime theory; links between transformation of resources into built environment, with a focus on housing, and accompanying flows (people, resources, waste, power); dynamics of socio-political power and domination in cities.

ARCH 390.name: Summer Practice II
ARCH 390.description: Practical experience in an architectural office; active participation in the design process and project development; observation of office environment (4 weeks).

ARCH 401.name: Architectural Design Studio V
ARCH 401.description: Embodies complex form generation based on architectural technologies that deal with building components and their interactions. Encourages the integration of technological advancements in construction and presentation techniques to the design process. Special consideration is given to contextual design, community leadership, participatory design and generation of building programs.

ARCH 402.name: Architectural Design Studio VI
ARCH 402.description: Emphasizes architectural complexity involving all relevant issues of a comprehensive design process including production drawings and documents; develops contemporary design solutions for a high-quality, sustainable and aesthetic built environment; focuses on multifunctional building design with complex programs in an urban context; physical and social integration of building into the urban texture.

ARCH 411.name: Conservation of Historical Environments
ARCH 411.description: General introduction to the principles and techniques of conservation and restoration; focuses on the problems and developments related to conservation in Turkey; covers analysis of restored historic sites and buildings.

ARCH 412.name: Studies in Historical Built Environment
ARCH 412.description: Presents case-based discussions on various topics concerning historical environments and their conservation, through lectures and practical exercises in studio.

ARCH 417.name: Advanced Visualization Studio
ARCH 417.description: Advanced techniques in computer aided visualization. Virtual environments, internet based platforms and software packages for design related disciplines are utilized for creating design visualizations.

ARCH 418.name: Professional Practice
ARCH 418.description: Professional administration of architectural design projects and the construction process; conduct of architectural practice; financial planning and contracts; professional ethics; rights and responsibilities of architects and clients; role of client and user; codes and legal aspects of building construction.

ARCH 420.name: Specialized Architectural Design Studio
ARCH 420.description: Specialized architectural design studio developing projects to be submitted to prestigious national and international design competitions.

ARCH 428.name: Integrated Design Management
ARCH 428.description: Execution of a multidisciplinary methodological approach to complex building design projects' process management; (re)-creation and reverse engineering of integrated design projects; focus on architectural priorities and management simulations throughout multiple correspondences, integrative and collaborative exchanges in synchronous design teams.

ARCH 440.name: Special Topics in Architectural Design
ARCH 440.description: Creation of a design project with a social content. Focus on architectural details and collaborative construction.

ARCH 462.name: Medieval Architecture in the Eastern Mediterranean
ARCH 462.description: Presents and evaluates the Byzantine Architectural heritage through a comparative approach; investigates the architectural context of the Byzantine world that expanded throughout the Eastern Mediterranean and emerged as one of the prominent architectural layers of the Anatolian peninsula. Provides a fuller understanding of the medieval period in the Eastern Mediterranean by opening comparative windows into the architectural characteristics of related medieval cultures such as Western Medieval, Early Islamic, Crusader, Seljuk, Beyliks etc.

ARCH 463.name: Modern Turkish Architecture
ARCH 463.description: Study of architectural developments in Turkey from 1900 to the present within a socio-cultural framework; particular emphasis on the interrelationship of architecture and political developments; survey of important buildings, key figures of architecture and urban design; extensive readings on the subject.

ARCH 465.name: Contemporary Architecture and Theory
ARCH 465.description: Review of the developments in Western architectural culture from the turn of the twentieth century to the present; contemporary architectural movements and theories.

ARCH 466.name: Architectural Theory and Criticism
ARCH 466.description: Investigation of architectural history, theory and criticism on special topics; social, cultural and political influences on architecture; readings of important theoretical and critical writings about a broad range of topics.

ARCH 511.name: Critical Issues in Heritage Studies
ARCH 511.description: Critical review of history of conservation, its origins, concepts, and shifting approaches; examination of contemporary debates and challenges related to interventions in architectural, urban, rural, and landscape heritage across different geographical contexts; investigation of multiple meanings, values, and decision-making processes that shape heritage practice today, with particular attention to current political, economic, social, cultural, and environmental dynamics.

ARCH 513.name: Theory and Methodology
ARCH 513.description: Deciphering and understanding approaches for analyzing the built environment. Evaluation and interpretation of texts related to architectural histories and theories.

ARCH 514.name: Architectural Readings
ARCH 514.description: Critical analyses of architectural texts; methods for analyzing architectural buildings; ways of deciphering digital and traditional (re)presentations of architecture.

ARCH 515.name: Topics in Architectural Technology
ARCH 515.description: A look at architectural technologies; digital opportunities, contemporary construction applications, developments in building materials.

ARCH 516.name: Computational Design Technologies
ARCH 516.description: Digital tools, media, digital geometries and parametric approaches that can be utilized in the process of producing architectural solutions.

ARCH 517.name: Advanced Visualization Studio
ARCH 517.description: Advanced techniques in computer aided visualization. Virtual environments, internet based platforms and software packages for design related disciplines utilized for creating design visualizations.

ARCH 550.name: Current Issues in Architectural Design
ARCH 550.description: A look at the contemporary buildings both from our geography and from abroad. Studies on the current architectural discussions.

ARCH 563.name: Modern Turkish Architecture
ARCH 563.description: Study of architectural developments in Turkey from 1900 to the present within a socio-cultural framework; particular emphasis on the interrelationship of architecture and political developments; survey of important buildings, key figures of architecture and urban design; extensive readings on the subject.

ARCH 564.name: Space and Culture
ARCH 564.description: Investigations on the relationship between culture and the built environment, including the work of architects, designers, and planners as well as the ordinary people who create our surroundings. Focus on the theoretical basis for architecture and cultural studies.

ARCH 565.name: Contemporary Architectural Discourse: Reading as Experimental Fieldwork
ARCH 565.description: Review of the developments in Western architectural culture from the turn of the twentieth century to the present; contemporary architectural movements and theories.

ARCH 566.name: Architectural Theory and Criticism
ARCH 566.description: Investigation of architectural history, theory and criticism on special topics; social, cultural and political influences on architecture; readings of important theoretical and critical writings about a broad range of topics.

ARCH 590.name: Graduate Seminar
ARCH 590.description: Academic presentations by graduate students on the theses they are preparing, answering relevant questions on the thesis; revisions.

ARCH 599.name: Master's Thesis
ARCH 599.description: Preparations towards the presentation of the thesis to the thesis jury, necessary format adjustments according to the Institute requirements.
